accuracy.evidence: Every function and derivative in the lab was recomputed: f = (x³ − 3x)/2 gives f′ = 1.5x² − 1.5 with zeros exactly at ±1 (f(−1) = 1, the maximum the prediction quotes); f = 1 − x²/2 gives −x; f = x⁴/4 − x² gives x³ − 2x, so the sketch targets at x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 are −4, 1, 0, −1, 4; sin(1.5x) gives 1.5cos(1.5x). The tangent drawn is y = f(a) + f′(a)(x − a). The three-pass method (zeros from turning points, sign from increasing/decreasing, size from steepness) matches the Khan Academy 'Connecting f and f′ graphically' unit and the A-level differentiation spec wording; items m2, m5 and p2 were evaluated at the corners of their parameter ranges by the items gate.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips in graphing f′ from f: plotting the zero at the height of the turning point (prediction 2 'At height 1', challenge tag height, p1, generated challenge), giving f′ the sign of f instead of its slope (prediction 3, sign step parts 1 and 2 feedback, m8, challenge fneg/fneg2), copying f and shifting it (match step 'copy' option, m6, challenge copy/copy2), putting a zero of f′ where f crosses the axis (p1, challenge height2), assuming a cubic's derivative is another cubic or a line (prediction 4, challenge copy/line) and confusing 'f′ decreasing' with 'f′ negative' (challenge shape).

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is built around two linked panels, f above and f′ below: dragging along f drops each tangent gradient as a dot at the same x on the f′ axes, then the learner marks zeros on the f′ axis, signs three intervals by tapping above or below it, drags five handles to sketch f′ of a W-shaped quartic, and matches f to one of three mini f′ plots. flagderiv (zooming in on a falling phone's distance curve) and flagtan (pivoting a ruler into the tangent of one distance-time graph) each find one gradient at one point and never build the graph of f′; gate_lab_distinct passes against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the rule before the text states it: the pink dots trace a U as they drag across the cubic, landing on the axis exactly under the hill and valley; tapping x = 0 in the zero step is refused with 'f is going down, not flat, so f′ is below the axis there (−1.5)'; signing the middle interval + is refused because f falls there even though it is above the axis; and the sketch check names which handle is off and whether by sign, flatness or steepness, before showing the true dashed f′.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options, each tested straight after: the gradient at a hilltop is 'as big as it gets' (the dot lands on the axis), the zero of f′ is 'at height 1' (it is at x = −1), f′ just right of the maximum is positive 'because f is above the axis' (the sign step rejects +), and a cubic's f′ is 'another cubic' (the match step shows the cubic option is f itself).

challenge_feedback.evidence: The challenge alternates a generated turning-points question (x-values change each time) with six fixed concept questions; each of the 13 wrong options has its own message, e.g. 'f′ records the slope, not the height. At a turning point the slope is 0', 'x² is never negative, but its slope is: for x < 0 the curve goes down, so f′ < 0', and 'Positive gradient, then negative, is up then down: a hill, so a maximum'. Generated items also state the working.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons reports the learner text at FK grade 2.4 (target 6.5) and the adult text at 6.1 (target 9.5). f′ is introduced as 'the gradient function' with the tangent picture first, step headings are short ('Turning points become zeros', 'Up means positive'), and canvas headers are live states such as 'x = −2: f is going up, gradient 4.5'.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs are one idea each in the order of the method: what f′ is, flat points, signs, size and the cubic example. Adult paragraphs add the three-pass method, shape rules by degree with the sine example, and the list of mistakes with a tangent spot-check. Lab copy is limited to instructions, live values and specific feedback.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of all seven steps after Show me in dark and light themes: both panels fit at 390 px with the f′ panel ranges chosen so every curve stays inside (cubic f′ peaks at 5.76 under a 6.5 cap, quartic handles at ±4 under ±7), x tick labels sit under the axis, the gradient pill flips below the point near the top edge, the match mini-plots are a third of the width each with A/B/C labels, and controls are 44 px wrapping buttons.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag or tap has a button: Left/Right to move the point, x = −2…2 to mark zeros, + above/− below for each part, Previous/Next point, Up/Down and Check for the sketch, A/B/C for matching, graph pickers and Show f′ in the sandbox. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with x, whether f is going up, down or flat, the gradient value or the feedback, and walk.cjs reports axe clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
